pages.title: Schedules and recurring bills
pages.description: Create schedules, let Purser materialize and match expected instances, and surface late bills and price changes.

sections.text: A schedule is a recurring expectation — the $60.00 gym membership on the 1st, the paycheck every other Friday. Purser materializes each schedule into expected transactions, matches them against what actually clears, and tells you when a bill is late or its price changed.

sections.heading: Create a schedule
sections.text: Recurrence is an RFC 5545 RRULE (the same syntax calendars use). Create a schedule on the admin UI's Schedules page (its cadence picker writes the rule for you), over REST (POST /schedules) or MCP with create schedule — an agent that parses a statement email calls this tool directly (Purser never parses email server-side). The schedule is created active. An agent acting on its own initiative passes propose=true instead, and the schedule lands as a suggestion that your decision turns into the schedule (decide suggestion). A proposal can carry a note (up to 200 characters, such as the statement line the agent read) for whoever decides it, and is refused when the account already has a schedule for that payee or counterparty. { "name": "Acme Gym", "account": "assets.checking", "rrule": "FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=1", "dtstart": "2026-09-01", "amount": "-60.00", "payee": "Acme Gym", "category": "expenses.personal.fitness" } Amounts are decimal strings; negative is money out. amount type defaults to fixed for a bill that is the same every period; estimated schedules take their amount from confirmed matches (estimate basis: last, rolling avg 3, rolling avg 12) with amount as the fallback before any history exists. Once two settled amounts differ, the forecast shows an estimated occurrence with its range — the lowest and highest of the last six together with the estimate (see Estimate range). dtstart is the rule's anchor — the date the recurrence counts from. Rules that name their day (BYMONTHDAY=6,20, BYDAY=FR) barely need it; rules that do not (FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2 — every other week) take their phase from it, so pass the last real occurrence. FREQ must be DAILY or coarser.

sections.heading: Recurring transfers
sections.text: A card payment, a loan payment, a 529 or IRA contribution is a transfer between two of your accounts, not a bill against a category. Give the schedule a counterparty account instead of a category: { "name": "Citi card payment", "account": "assets.checking", "counterparty account": "liabilities.citicard", "rrule": "FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=5", "dtstart": "2026-09-05", "amount type": "estimated", "estimate basis": "counterparty balance" } Its instances are two-leg expected transfers — the schedule account's leg is amount (negative = money leaves it), the counterparty's leg the opposite — so they show up in both accounts' forecasts, and when the bank rows on both sides arrive and link into one transfer, the matcher settles the expectation against that merged row (no double count). The schedule is itself what links those rows when their descriptors say nothing about a transfer, and the two sides may post on different days — see Scheduled transfers. The counterparty balance basis sizes each instance from the counterparty's reported balance: "pay the card in full". For a card that is the current balance, charges since the statement closed included, so record the statement when it arrives (next section). The whats new week of upcoming bills reads an instance from the schedule account's leg, the side that pays: a card or loan payment due this week is listed with its (negative) amount and counts toward the total, while a transfer into the schedule's account (a sweep from savings, say) is money arriving, not a bill.

sections.heading: Card statement balances
sections.text: A card payment estimated from the card's current balance usually runs high: you pay the statement balance from the last close, and the card has new charges since. Purser cannot read statements (SimpleFIN carries no statement figure), so you or your agent record it against the payment it is due on — on the Schedules page ( Statement on a card payment's instance), over REST, or with MCP record statement balance. An agent reading a statement email ("statement balance 8,347.00, payment due October 19") makes one call: { "account": "liabilities.citicard", "statement balance": "8347.00", "due date": "2026-10-19", "statement date": "2026-09-22" } statement balance is the figure as printed: the amount owed, positive. Purser finds the card's live payment instance due nearest due date (within 14 days), sets it to the statement balance on both legs (-8347.00 from checking), and pins it, so the current-balance estimate no longer moves it; the next cycle's payment keeps following the balance. Over REST (POST /schedules/statement-balance) you can name the instance by transaction id instead of account and due date. The statement, its closing date and who recorded it stay on the instance, the instance and the forecast report basis: statement, and recording again replaces the figure. Reset the instance to go back to the current balance. Recording needs write scope and works on credit card payments only; a loan payment, or any other bill, is an ordinary override (below). Paying the exact statement amount also lets the schedule link the payment's bank rows (it vouches only for its exact amount).

sections.heading: Rules and instances
sections.text: The schedule is the durable rule . What you actually see in a register and in the forecast are its instances : expected transactions materialized on a rolling 60-day horizon, nightly and whenever a schedule is activated or edited. Each instance fills one slot of the rule (its occurrence date), and materialization never creates a second instance for a slot that already has one — matched, skipped, or edited. Instances are yours to edit; the rule never overrides what you touched: - Override an occurrence — a different amount ("this month's card payment is 8,067.37") or date ("it lands on the 3rd") — with the ordinary transaction edit (PATCH /transactions/{id}, MCP override instance). The instance becomes pinned : estimate refreshes and rule edits leave it alone. On a transfer schedule both legs move: the amount is the schedule account's leg in the schedule's sign (-8067.37 for a card payment from checking), or the leg of the account a PATCH names in account ({"amount": "8067.37", "account": "liabilities.citicard"} from the card's side). An amount whose sign would reverse the transfer is refused. A card's statement balance has its own path, which keeps the statement on the instance (see Card statement balances). - Relabel an occurrence — a different description or payee. A label is not an override: the instance stays un-pinned and keeps following the estimate. - Reset an overridden occurrence (POST /transactions/{id}/reset-instance, MCP reset instance, write scope; the Reset button on a pinned row in the Schedules page). The pin is cleared and the instance takes the rule's date (its slot), name, payee and current estimate again, and a recorded card statement is removed. If the rule no longer has that slot, or estimates nothing, the instance is dropped instead. - Skip an occurrence (POST /transactions/{id}/void, MCP skip instance). The slot stays filled, so the occurrence does not come back. - Mark paid by matching the instance to a posted row (POST /matching/match, MCP match). When the matcher already proposed that very pair, this confirms the proposal — the unmatched report (GET /matching/unmatched, MCP list unmatched) names the proposed bank row as proposed posted id — and a row proposed for a different bill is refused, with the error naming that bill. The rule side: an estimated schedule refreshes its live, un-pinned instances whenever a new confirmed match moves the estimate (audited as schedule.refresh). Editing the rule (PATCH /schedules/{id}, MCP update schedule) resyncs: slots the new rule no longer produces are voided and released, survivors are re-estimated, missing slots materialize — and editing back re-fills the released slots. Renaming a schedule (or changing its payee) relabels its live instances, pinned ones too: every instance whose description is still the old name takes the new one, and so does a payee that is still the old one — a schedule without a payee uses its name as its instances' payee. A description or payee you set yourself is kept. Pause stops expecting (live un-pinned instances are dropped and come back on resume ); end is terminal and keeps history (POST /schedules/{id}/pause, /resume, /end; MCP end schedule with action set to pause, resume or end). GET /schedules/{id} lists the live instances with their slot, pinned and overdue flags; next due is always the earliest live instance — an overdue one counts, because it is still due. In the admin UI the same actions live on the Schedules page (expand a schedule for its instances; pinned rows carry Reset) and on the account register, where a materialized row carries a scheduled badge with Override, Mark paid and Skip.

sections.heading: Expected instances and matching
sections.text: The matcher reconciles each instance against the real posted or pending row when it arrives. The posted amount always wins — the expectation is replaced by reality, and the difference is recorded as a variance. Variance feeds future estimates, and a breach beyond the threshold emits a variance.threshold event. A match to a pending row follows that row. When the bank posts it, the match moves to the posted row and the bill stays paid (a proposed match is decided again against the posted row). If the bank drops the pending instead, the match is released and the instance comes back as expected, in the same slot and with any override you made, so it can go late or match the charge the bank really posts. Voiding the pending yourself (POST /transactions/{id}/void) does the same: a confirmed match is released the same way, and a proposed match is withdrawn so the bill can be matched again. While a match is only proposed , the bank row is already in the balance, so the forecast and the whats new week of upcoming bills treat the instance as paid, pending your confirmation, and the forecast's coverage counts it in matches pending. Estimates only learn from posted amounts: a pending amount can still change, so it moves the estimate (and raises a recurring.price changed event) only once the posted row lands — whether the bank posts it, you post the pending yourself (POST /transactions/{id}/post), or the bank's posted row for the other side of a pending transfer arrives and posts the whole transfer.

sections.heading: Late bills
sections.text: When an expected instance passes its window unmatched, Purser emits a bill.late event. Late bills surface three ways: the event stream (and any webhook), the whats new MCP digest, and the Dashboard's Needs attention card, which collects late bills alongside the suggestions awaiting your decision. A late bill the matcher has proposed a bank row for shows as that proposal's match card instead: accept it to mark the bill paid, or reject it so that row is never proposed for the bill again.

sections.heading: Low-balance warnings
sections.text: To be warned before an account runs low, give it a floor: in the app, Set floor in the account's register header; over REST, PATCH /accounts/{id} with {"min balance": "500.00"}; or have your agent call update account(account, min balance="500.00"). Each night Purser projects the next 30 days of every account with a floor, schedules included, and emits a forecast.shortfall event when the projection drops below it. Clear the floor (null, or "" in update account) to stop the warnings. See Shortfalls for the sign rules and which account types take a floor.

sections.heading: Detected schedules
sections.text: Purser also proposes schedules it finds for you. Every night (and on POST /schedules/detect / MCP detect schedules) it scans your history per account and counterparty — a payee for ordinary bills, the other account for transfers such as card payments, loan payments and contributions — and each recurring pattern becomes a suggestion in the suggestions inbox with the evidence attached: the occurrences, the cadence it found (weekly, every two weeks, semi-monthly, monthly, every two/three/six months, yearly), how regular the gaps were, and how steady the amount was. A varying amount is not a veto — card payments that swing threefold are still monthly; they come through as estimated (paying the card's balance when the counterparty is a card). A single skipped month is tolerated; a pattern that stopped is not proposed. Adding a credit card or loan account triggers the same scan for payments to it right away (source = account added). Detected patterns never auto-activate — accepting the suggestion is the only path to an active schedule, and rejecting one is remembered.

sections.heading: Price changes
sections.text: list recurring is the subscription radar: every active outflow schedule with an honest monthly-equivalent total (annual and semi-annual bills normalized), its next due date, and its last price change, all computed server-side — never sum the rows yourself. A schedule you accepted from a suggestion is as active as one you created: its source (manual, detected or agent) only records where it came from. Patterns still waiting for your decision are not listed; suggestions open counts them, and they live in the suggestions inbox. In MCP Apps hosts the recurring widget shows that count as a footer. When a recurring charge posts at a new amount, Purser emits a recurring.price changed event and the change lands in that price history, so "what am I paying, and what changed?" is one tool call. The authoritative spec is DESIGN.md sections 6 (schedules and forecasting) and 5 (matching). See the MCP tool catalog for list recurring, create schedule, update schedule, end schedule, skip instance, override instance, reset instance and record statement balance. Recurrence detection counts each correction chain once, using its latest replacement. Editing a posted bank transaction does not double its amount in the history, whether the correction was made by a person, an agent or a rule.

pages.title: Connect banks with SimpleFIN
pages.description: Claim a SimpleFIN setup token, map feed accounts to the ledger, schedule syncs, backfill history, and scope each account with feed_start.

sections.text: SimpleFIN Bridge is Purser's live feed path: an aggregator hands the Bridge your bank data, and Purser fetches it on a schedule. Every payload is archived verbatim to the append-only raw fetches archive before anything touches the ledger, and every imported row traces back to those bytes. A row's identity is its content — account, date, amount and description — never the bank's transaction id, which can change between fetches. Two identical charges on one day (the same merchant, the same amount) are still two rows: within one fetch, the second identical row is the second occurrence of that content, an identity of its own. Every sync re-fetches the last seven days so pending charges can settle, and that overlap adds nothing, because each fetch numbers its identical rows from one again and lands on identities already in the ledger.

sections.heading: Connect
sections.text: Get a setup token from your SimpleFIN Bridge account page and paste it into the first-run wizard, or later into Config - SimpleFIN . Setup tokens are one-time secrets — paste them only into Purser, never into a chat. Purser exchanges the token once for an encrypted access URL (stored encrypted at rest; it never appears in logs) and discovers the accounts the connection exposes.

sections.heading: Map feed accounts to ledger accounts
sections.text: Discovered feed accounts are not ledger accounts until you map them. In Config - SimpleFIN , map each one to a Purser account (or create the account inline). Only mapped accounts sync. Closing a ledger account unmaps it, and the feed account reappears as unmapped — reopen and remap to resume.

sections.heading: Sync schedule and the fetch budget
sections.text: The schedule is a runtime setting in Config - SimpleFIN (not an environment variable): daily at 06:30 UTC (default), every 12h , every 6h , or hourly . Every preset lands a run just before the matching job. SimpleFIN Bridge allows 24 fetches per day ; the hourly preset sits exactly at that budget, and the per-connection guard fails soft beyond it. Agents should call trigger sync when the user wants fresh data, not on every question.

sections.heading: Pending transactions
sections.text: Banks report a charge as pending before it posts, and Purser imports it as a pending row. Every sync re-checks each open pending on a checking, savings, cash or credit card account against the bank, not only the last week's: the fetch reaches back to the oldest such pending (and a week before it), up to the 90 days one fetch can cover. Pendings on brokerage, loan and property accounts never stretch the fetch: some investment feeds list every purchase as pending indefinitely, and those accounts are valued by holdings or valuations anyway. They are still settled whenever the fetch covers their dates. - When the bank posts it, the posted row replaces the pending, whether it arrives with a new description or date or with the very same ones. - When a pending disappears, Purser first looks for its posted row: same account, same amount, dated within 7 days either way. - A pending the bank dropped with no posted row is voided and emits a pending.vanished event. The whats new digest counts these and lists the ones above its materiality threshold. A dropped refund is worth chasing. A pending older than 90 days is beyond what the bridge serves and stays as it is. Void it yourself if your bank no longer shows it.

sections.heading: Re-described rows
sections.text: A fetch that reaches back past the last week also brings older posted rows the ledger already holds. Banks sometimes rewrite a posted row's description weeks later (a merchant name gains a suffix, say), and because the description is part of a row's identity, that copy would otherwise land as a second row. Purser skips it as re-described when the account already has a posted row from an earlier sync on the same date for the same amount, under a description the bank no longer lists. Sync and backfill results count these as skipped redescribed. A row that posted late with no such neighbour imports normally, and so does a row a disappearing pending may have posted as.

sections.heading: Backfill older history
sections.text: An incremental sync only reaches about 90 days back. To page older history, use Fetch older history in Config (or POST /connections/{id}/backfill, write scope). Backfill walks backward in windows of at most 90 days, archiving each verbatim, and latches complete after two consecutive empty windows. It never moves the forward sync anchor, shares the daily fetch budget (reserving two fetches for scheduled and manual syncs), and resumes from a saved cursor if interrupted. A result may carry a qif overlap warning when a backfilled range meets manually imported rows; identical rows still dedup by content hash. You can scope a backfill to specific accounts so onboarding one need not re-fetch the rest.

sections.heading: Scope an account with feed_start
sections.text: accounts.feed start is a per-account date: the importer skips feed rows dated strictly before it, across sync, backfill, and map re-import alike. Set it to partition an account's history cleanly — manual import owns everything before the boundary, the feed owns everything on or after it. It is import-time only: setting it never deletes rows already in the ledger, and skips are counted as skipped before feed start. Set it via PATCH /accounts/{id} (an explicit null clears it). The typical rollout is to set it at the manual/feed boundary when you first map the account.

sections.heading: Fix a sign-inverted feed with feed_invert
sections.text: Some institutions deliver an account's transaction stream with the signs flipped — deposits arriving as negative amounts (observed with Fidelity brokerage, HSA, and 401(k) accounts). The symptoms are an asset account whose balance trends negative and transfers that never pair (both legs carry the same sign). Set accounts.feed invert via PATCH /accounts/{id} (admin, like feed start) and the importer negates every feed amount for that account from then on. The inversion happens after content hashing, so a row's identity stays exactly what the bank sent: flipping the flag never re-imports history, and rows already in the ledger are never rewritten — repairing existing wrong-signed rows is a separate, deliberate admin operation.

sections.heading: Loan and property balances come from valuations
sections.text: A loan or mortgage feed often reports a balance but few or no transactions. Purser records each reported balance for a loan or property account as a row in that account's valuations series, and every balance surface — the accounts list, the account page headline, GET /accounts/{id}/balance, and the agent tools — reports the latest valuation as the account's balance (balance method: "valuation", with balance as of naming the valuation date). When the feed does deliver transactions they stay visible in the register as ordinary postings history, and the postings sum rides along as postings balance. An account with no valuation yet falls back to the postings sum. Net worth uses the same rule, so the account page and net worth always agree.

sections.heading: Brokerage balances add holdings to cash
sections.text: A brokerage feed reports cash transactions and a holdings snapshot side by side. Purser stores each as what it is — cash movements become ordinary postings, holdings become rows in holdings snapshots — and every balance surface reports the two added together : the postings sum plus the market value of the latest holdings snapshot at or before the date you asked about (balance method: "postings+holdings", with balance as of naming the snapshot date). The cash-only figure rides along as postings balance. The difference from a loan is that a valuation replaces the postings sum while a market value adds to it — a brokerage account's cash is real money the feed already told you about, so dropping it would understate the account. An account with no snapshot yet reports the postings sum alone, and a closed account keeps its postings answer so a stale snapshot cannot resurrect it. Net worth uses the same rule, so the account page and net worth agree here too. See Balances for all three methods and the two bases they are applied to.

sections.heading: When the feed sends no holdings
sections.text: Some brokerage feeds deliver the account's cash but no holdings at all. Switch such an account's holdings source to manual (admin, PATCH /accounts/{id} with {"holdings source": "manual"}) and record its positions by hand: the feed keeps importing the cash, stops recording holdings for that account (holdings skipped manual in the sync result), and the positions you record are priced daily and added to the balance the same way. See Track holdings by hand.

sections.heading: Watch accounts converge
sections.text: Config - SimpleFIN shows a Feed accounts table fed by GET /connections/{id}/discovered: per account, the feed-reported balance date, the ledger balance, and any drift between them, recomputed live from the latest archived payload. It is the convergence meter while you onboard or backfill — expect drift to shrink toward zero as history fills in. After every successful sync, Purser also runs a balance-drift check that emits a balance.drift event when a mapped cash or card account's reported balance disagrees with the ledger. It is a warning only : it never fails a sync, never adjusts the ledger, and never writes financial rows. See Events and webhooks for the event, and whats new for the agent-facing digest. When the drift is real and you have the statement balance, reconcile the account. Banks differ on whether the balance they report counts pending charges, so the drift is measured on the basis each account's bank uses, reported as drift basis and shown next to the drift: posted only when the bank leaves pendings out, pending inclusive otherwise. Purser learns the basis per account from its recent syncs (the one whose drift held steady wins), so a standing gap at a bank that leaves pendings out stays one number while charges come and go instead of moving with every pending. The same basis rides on the balance.drift event (mode) and on each whats new drift line (basis). An account's first syncs have nothing to learn from yet, so the smaller of the two drifts decides until its history tells them apart. The ledger balance column always includes pendings.

sections.heading: Pin an account's drift basis
sections.text: When an account's history is short or misleading, pin its basis by hand: the Basis select in the Feed accounts table offers Auto (showing the basis Purser learned) and the two pins. Over the API, an admin sends PATCH /accounts/{id} with {"drift basis override": "posted only"} or "pending inclusive"; null clears the pin and absent leaves it alone. Only checking, savings, cash and credit-card accounts take a pin (the drift check runs on nothing else), and the change is audited. A pinned basis wins over the learned one everywhere it is reported: GET /connections/{id}/discovered sets drift basis pinned (and still shows the learned pick as drift basis learned), the balance.drift event carries basis pinned: true, and the whats new drift line carries pinned: true. The pin only chooses which drift is reported: an account whose bank balance matches either basis is still in sync. Purser keeps learning underneath the pin, so clearing it brings back exactly the basis its history picks. Because setting or clearing a pin changes the reported drift, it can open one new balance.drift episode. The authoritative spec is DESIGN.md sections 7.1 (connect, backfill, feed start) and 7.3 (balance-drift check).

pages.title: Suggestions inbox
pages.description: Decide what Purser thinks you should do — detected recurring bills and transfers, agent-proposed schedules, transfer-link rules your confirms propose, bill matches the matcher proposes — from the Dashboard cards or the MCP tools.

sections.text: A suggestion is something Purser thinks you should decide: a recurring payee it found in your history, a schedule an agent proposed, a payment for a card you just added, a rule to link a transfer you keep confirming by hand, or a bank row the matcher thinks paid one of your expected bills. It carries a typed draft of what it would create, the evidence behind it, a confidence where Purser scored one, and it remembers what you decided. The Dashboard cards and the MCP tools are two renderings of the same rows. Every suggestion has a kind, and the kind decides what its draft is: Kind Draft Accepting it creates --- --- --- schedule a schedule (name, account, rrule, amount, ...) an active schedule, materialized immediately transfer link a transfer link rule for one account pair, scoped to a payee the rule as a draft , which links nothing until you activate it match an expected row and the bank row the matcher proposed for it, with both amounts and the variance the confirmed match : the bill is paid by that row

sections.heading: Where suggestions come from
sections.text: - Detection. The nightly detector (07:05 UTC), POST /schedules/detect or MCP detect schedules scans your history per account and counterparty — payees for ordinary bills, the other account for transfers — for recurring cadences (weekly to yearly, including semi-monthly paydays). Each pattern becomes one suggestion — never a schedule — with a confidence that reflects how much evidence there is, how regular the gaps are and how steady the amount is. Running detection again refreshes the open row (its seen count climbs) instead of creating a duplicate. - Agents. A create schedule call with propose=true lands here with the draft the agent asked for, source = agent. It has no confidence, because nothing scored it, so it lists after the scored suggestions. The agent can attach a note of up to 200 characters, such as the statement line it read, and the card shows it. If the account already has a schedule for that payee or counterparty (active, paused or ended), the proposal is refused with a 422 that names the schedule, so the inbox never holds a duplicate of it. - A new liability account (card, loan) triggers a scan for payments to it — merged transfers to the account and one-sided outflows whose payee names it — and lands them as source = account added. - A manual transfer confirm. When you merge two bank rows with confirm transfer (MCP) or POST /matching/confirm-transfer, Purser proposes a transfer link rule for that account pair, scoped to the payee on the rows, as source = confirm. Confirming another pair of the same accounts and payee refreshes the same suggestion — its evidence is the pairs you confirmed — instead of adding one. A split loan payment proposes nothing, and neither does a pair whose rows carry no payee. See Manage transfers. - The matcher. When the nightly matching pass (or POST /matching/run) scores a bank row in the middle tier for an expected bill — close, but not sure enough to match on its own — it proposes the match and the proposal appears here as a match card (source = detected, the match score as its confidence). The card only mirrors the proposal: confirming or rejecting it in an account register, or marking the bill paid with that row, decides the card too, and when the proposal goes away on its own — the bank drops the pending row, the row merges into a transfer, a better row settles the bill — the card is withdrawn . A bank row matched to an expected transfer waits a few days for its other leg before it gets a card, because the transfer usually settles it by itself. See How matching works.

sections.heading: Deciding
sections.text: POST /suggestions/{id}/decide or MCP decide suggestion, write scope: Decision Effect --- --- accept Applies the draft exactly as shown. A schedule becomes an active schedule, materialized immediately; a transfer link becomes a draft rule (below); a match confirms the match, which also marks the bank row reviewed. edit then accept Same, after merging your edits. A schedule takes any draft field — name, rrule, dtstart, amount, amount type, estimate basis, payee, category, counterparty account, autopost policy. A transfer link takes only what narrows or widens it — amount exact (a decimal string), window days (0 to 14) and effective from — because its account pair and payee are what it proposes. A match has nothing to edit: to pay the bill with a different row, mark it paid with that row (POST /matching/match, MCP match). The edits are validated by the same schema before anything is created. reject Durable. reject scope = counterparty means "never suggest this payee or counterparty on this account again" — for a transfer link, never again for this account pair, whatever the payee; exact (default) rejects just this pattern, or this pair and payee. A match is rejected exactly: the matcher never proposes that bank row for that bill again, nor the posted row that replaces it when it was pending. snooze Hides it until snooze until (default 30 days). Nothing auto-accepts on expiry — it simply returns to the inbox. A snoozed match stays proposed: its bank row is still held, and the forecast still counts the bill as paid pending your confirmation. Deciding a match card whose proposal is already gone answers 422 and withdraws the card.

sections.heading: Accepting a transfer link
sections.text: A transfer-link suggestion never links anything by itself, and accepting it does not either. Accepting creates the rule as a draft and returns projected links: how many of your past pairs the rule would link if you activated it now. Activation is the rule's own confirm step — the Dashboard card asks it right after you accept, the Rules page offers it for every draft, and over REST it is POST /rules/{rule id}/state with {"state": "active", "confirm links": N}. An agent can accept with decide suggestion, but there is no MCP tool to activate the rule: the count confirm happens on the Dashboard card, the Rules page or over REST. See Activating a pair rule for why the count is asked for. On the Dashboard each open suggestion is a card: the headline, its source and confidence, an evidence summary that expands into the occurrences (or, for a transfer link, the pairs you confirmed), and the four decisions (rejecting asks whether to reject just this one or never suggest the pair again). GET /suggestions lists the open inbox by confidence — ?kind=schedule, ?kind=transfer link or ?kind=match narrows it, and ?status=withdrawn shows the cards Purser closed on its own; GET /suggestions/{id} adds the full evidence. A match card shows the expected row against the bank row and the variance, with Accept, Snooze and Reject. MCP list suggestions (with an optional kind) returns the same rows with a one-line headline, the draft, an evidence summary (count, first/last, amount range, cadence, and an agent's note) and the confidence; whats new carries the open count and the top few.

sections.heading: Why it remembers
sections.text: Every suggestion has a stable fingerprint — the account it lives on plus who it is with (a payee, or a counterparty account); for a transfer link, the two accounts in either order plus the payee. One row per fingerprint, ever: a pattern found tomorrow lands on the same row, a pattern you rejected last week stays rejected, and a pattern already covered by one of your schedules — or a pair and payee one of your transfer link rules already covers — is never suggested at all. That is what keeps the inbox from becoming noise. A match's fingerprint is the bill's schedule slot (or the expected row) plus the bank row, so rejecting it holds even when the bill comes back as a fresh copy in the same slot. A transfer link's payee is matched through its aliases : if a rename rule later merges that payee into a friendlier one, a confirm under the new name still refreshes the same suggestion, and a rejection still holds. The authoritative spec is DESIGN.md section 6 (schedules and forecasting) and decisions 57, 67 and 86. Schedules themselves are covered in Schedules and recurring bills, rules in Write deterministic rules.

pages.title: Manage transfers
pages.description: How Purser links the two sides of a transfer deterministically, when it asks first, and how to convert, absorb, and unlink.

sections.text: A transfer between your own accounts is not spending. In Purser it is one transaction with two real-account postings — money leaving assets.checking and arriving in assets.savings — not two unrelated rows. Getting the two bank sides joined into that single transaction is what this page is about. A loan payment whose bank sides differ by its interest is the one variation: it adds a single interest/fee posting (see Confirm a split loan payment).

sections.heading: Deterministic auto-linking
sections.text: At import (and on the daily sweep), Purser looks for opposite-amount pairs across accounts whose dates are at most 3 days apart. A pair is auto-linked only when the amount-and-window match is joined by a signal : - a name signal — a transfer or payment-style keyword (transfer, xfer, payment, autopay, ...) or the counterparty account's own name in the text; - a declared pair — an active transfer link rule for the two accounts, which can also give that pair its own window (see Declared pairs and their window); - a scheduled transfer — a transfer schedule's instance covers the pair (see Scheduled transfers below). When a signal is present the two one-sided rows merge into a single transfer and the originals are voided with links back. This is deterministic by design — no scoring, no guessing. Every auto-merge is logged, evented, badged, and reversible : it writes an audit row, emits a transfer.auto linked event whose signal names what linked it — rule:<rule id , name or schedule:<schedule id , the first that applies — shows a badge in the register, and can be undone with unlink. The auto path acts on posted rows only ; pending pairs stay confirm-first until they post. Turn it off entirely with the PURSER TRANSFER AUTO LINK setting (Config - Settings, default on) — then every candidate waits for you.

sections.heading: Scheduled transfers
sections.text: A transfer schedule — a monthly savings sweep, a 529 contribution — already says which two accounts move how much, and when. That is enough to link its bank rows, even when their descriptors carry no keyword at all (FID BKG SVC LLC MONEYLINE on one side, MONEY LINE RECEIVED EFT on the other). A pair is covered when an instance of an active transfer schedule: - names the same two accounts, in the same direction; - has exactly the pair's amount — an estimated instance whose amount differs from the bank's is not a signal; link those by name, by rule, or by confirming; - is dated within the 3-day window of both legs. The bank legs of a transfer often post a day or more apart, and the nightly job matches expectations before it links transfers, so the first leg is usually matched to the instance by the time its counterpart arrives — proposed when only the amount and date agree, matched outright when the description agrees too. That leg stays linkable: a bank row matched to an expected transfer still pairs with a row on that transfer's other account (never with anything else), so the pair links whichever side posts first. Either way the instance ends up settled once, by the merged transfer : a confirmed match moves onto the merge, a proposal is replaced by an automatic match on it, and an instance that was still open is matched to the merge at link time. The merged transfer is then matched, so no other expectation can claim it. A bank row matched to an ordinary bill is never pulled into a transfer this way. When an estimated instance is off — the card statement says 8,347.00, not the balance the schedule estimated — override the instance to the statement amount (Rules and instances). Both of its legs move, and an instance at exactly the bank's amount is a signal again, so the payment links when its bank rows arrive.

sections.heading: Confirm-first candidates
sections.text: An amount-and-window pair with no signal is a transfer.candidate event, not an auto-link: it looks like a transfer but Purser will not merge it silently. Confirm it yourself — confirm transfer over MCP, or the register's confirm control — to merge the pair, or leave it as two categorized rows. A bank row already matched to an expected transfer is still listed with its counterpart, and confirming the pair carries the match onto the transfer.

sections.heading: From a confirm to a rule
sections.text: A confirm merges that one pair and teaches Purser nothing hidden. What it does instead is visible: it proposes a transfer link rule for the two accounts, scoped to the payee on the rows, as a suggestion in the suggestions inbox. The confirm's response carries its suggestion id. Confirm another pair between the same accounts with the same payee, in either direction, and the same suggestion is refreshed, with each pair you confirmed listed as its evidence. Nothing links because of the suggestion until you decide it: - Accept creates the rule as a draft and tells you how many past pairs it would link. Activating it asks you to confirm that count — the same confirmation as any pair rule. Once active, pairs between those accounts where one side carries the payee (or an alias of it) link on their own, past and future. - Edit and accept narrows or widens the draft first: an exact amount, a date window of 0 to 14 days, or a start date. - Reject is remembered: that pair and payee are never proposed again, or, with "never for this pair", that account pair with any payee. - Snooze brings it back after 30 days. Unlinking a pair you confirmed undoes that merge and nothing else. The suggestion stays in the inbox for you to decide, and no rule exists until you accept one, so the next pair from the same payee stays a confirm-first candidate. A split loan payment proposes no rule, since its unequal sides could never link automatically, and neither does a pair whose rows carry no payee: one confirm is not evidence about every transfer between two accounts.

sections.heading: Declared pairs and their window
sections.text: When two of your accounts transfer to each other regularly but the bank text carries no signal, declare the pair with a transfer link rule — or accept the one a confirm proposed. For that pair the name signal is no longer needed, and the rule can also set the pair's own date window with window days (0 to 14 days; 3 when unset). A card autopay whose two sides post 4 days apart links once its pair rule has window days of 4 or more, while every pair you have not declared keeps the 3-day window. A wider window never takes a row from a closer pair already in your ledger: each pass links everything within 3 days first, exactly as it would without the rule, and pairs the declared accounts farther apart only among the rows left without a partner. Activating the rule asks you to confirm how many historical pairs it will link, counted with its window.

sections.heading: Confirm a split loan payment
sections.text: A loan payment rarely shows the same amount on both sides. Checking reports the whole payment leaving; the loan account reports only the principal it was paid down by; the difference is interest or fees. Those two rows never auto-link (every automatic path needs exactly opposite amounts), so confirm them yourself and name the category the difference belongs to: curl -sX POST https://purser.example.com/matching/confirm-transfer \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $PURSER TOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"outgoing id": "CHECKING ROW ID", "incoming id": "LOAN ROW ID", "remainder category": "expenses.fees.interest"}' Over MCP, call confirm transfer with the same three arguments. With checking at -612.40 and the loan at +540.15, Purser records one transaction: Posting Amount --- --- assets.checking (the bank's cash leg, unchanged) -612.40 liabilities.carloan (the loan's principal leg, unchanged) 540.15 expenses.fees.interest (the remainder) 72.25 It sums to zero by construction, and it never invents a full-payment 612.40 posting on the loan — each bank leg stays exactly what its bank reported. The response, the audit row and the transfer.confirmed event carry the remainder and its remainder category. The rules: - The incoming (principal) amount must be positive and smaller than the outgoing (cash) amount. Equal legs are an ordinary transfer — confirm them without remainder category. A principal larger than the cash, a zero, or a negative leg is refused with a 422 that names the problem. - remainder category must be an expense category, and not expenses.uncategorized. - It needs write scope, and nothing automatic ever does it — no auto-link, absorb, rule or AI path produces a split. - Unlink restores both bank rows exactly as they were, and the interest posting goes with the split. To change the category, unlink and confirm again. In the register the row shows the other account as its [account] value, with a split line under it giving the remainder amount and category. Over the API the row carries is transfer: true, transfer account path, category path (the remainder category) and remainder amount; MCP search transactions rows carry counterparty, category and remainder. Only the shapes Purser writes count as transfers: a row that touches two real accounts and several categories is shown as what it is, not as a transfer.

sections.heading: Convert a row into a transfer
sections.text: In the flat view a transfer's "category" is the other account in Quicken-style brackets, and the same sugar works for writes. Set a row's category to [assets.savings] (via update transaction or a PATCH) to convert it into a transfer to that account. Depending on what already exists on the other side, the conversion absorbs into a matching transfer, merges with a live one-sided counterpart (including one already matched to an expected transfer between the same two accounts — the match moves onto the merge), or converts in place. Set a plain category back to undo it, naming in account the side that keeps the row. A conversion must be the only change in the call, and a transfer carrying linked bank rows must be unlinked first.

sections.heading: Change a transfer's amount
sections.text: An expected or pending transfer takes a new amount in place: send amount with account naming the side it is read from, and both legs move (a schedule instance defaults to its schedule's account). The direction never changes — an amount whose sign would reverse the transfer is refused. A transfer carrying linked bank rows, a split loan payment and a posted transfer are not edited this way: unlink them so their bank rows come back as separate transactions (convert a posted transfer without bank rows back to a category instead).

sections.heading: Absorb and unlink
sections.text: Absorb handles the late-arriving side: when an imported row matches an existing transfer's unbacked side and carries a name signal (or the pair is declared, within the rule's window), it is voided into that transfer instead of duplicating it (a transfer.absorbed event). Unlink undoes a link — the merged transfer splits back into its one-sided originals (with their content hashes moved onto the resurrected rows) and a transfer.unlinked event fires. If the transfer settled an expectation, such as a scheduled transfer's instance, that settlement goes with it: the instance is due again in its slot and the next matching run decides what settles it — it is never brought back as a posted copy. A pair you explicitly unlinked is suppressed from the auto paths only; an explicit confirm or convert can always relink it. The authoritative spec is DESIGN.md sections 5 (matching and transfer tiers) and 3.3 (bracket transfers and split loan payments). See Events and webhooks for the transfer events.

pages.title: CLI
pages.description: One image, multiple roles — purser serve, worker, migrate, plus keygen, seed-demo, and guarded admin commands.

sections.text: The purser command is the single entrypoint for every role. All role commands fail fast without a valid PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY , and a wrong-key canary check fails closed before anything serves.

sections.heading: purser serve
sections.text: Apply migrations, then serve the API, the MCP endpoint, the admin SPA, and the in-process job scheduler. The default single-process deployment.

sections.heading: purser worker
sections.text: Run only the scheduled jobs (sync, matching, forecasting, retention). For the optional role split: run serve with PURSER DISABLE SCHEDULER=true alongside one worker — same image, same configuration.

sections.heading: purser migrate
sections.text: Apply database migrations to head and exit. serve and worker migrate on startup, so this exists for init containers and manual control. Every role holds a Postgres advisory lock while it upgrades, so processes that start together (a serve + worker split) take turns instead of racing: the later one waits, logs that it is waiting, then finds the schema already at head.

sections.heading: purser keygen
sections.text: Print a fresh Fernet key for PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY.

sections.heading: purser seed-demo
sections.text: Seed a small realistic demo dataset: a few accounts, two months of synthetic transactions, a transfer pair, one recurring bill and one card-payment transfer schedule — enough to exercise matching, forecasting, and every read tool without a bank connection. Skips silently when the database already holds user data — any real (non-category) account or any transaction. --force seeds anyway and writes a seed.force audit row.

sections.heading: Guarded admin commands
sections.text: Offline remediation. Back up first.

sections.heading: purser admin delete-account
sections.text: purser admin delete-account <path-or-uuid dry-run pre-flight report purser admin delete-account <path-or-uuid --yes execute Hard-delete a duplicate account and free its content hashes for re-import. Dry-run by default; refuses virtual, SimpleFIN-attached, and parent accounts. The append-only raw feed archive is never touched. This is deliberately a CLI, not an API — no token scope can delete an account.

sections.heading: purser admin purge-feed-rows
sections.text: purser admin purge-feed-rows <path-or-uuid dry-run report purser admin purge-feed-rows <path-or-uuid --since 2026-05-01 bounded purser admin purge-feed-rows <path-or-uuid --yes execute Hard-delete an account's feed-origin rows (any status) so the archive can re-derive them — the repair half-step for feed data that imported wrong, such as a sign-inverted stream. QIF, manual, and agent rows are never touched; merge-linked transfers unlink first so the counterpart's bank line survives; the raw feed archive stays whole. Dry-run by default. Follow with replay-archive.

sections.heading: purser admin replay-archive
sections.text: purser admin replay-archive <connection-uuid plan only purser admin replay-archive <connection-uuid --since 2026-07-01 bounded purser admin replay-archive <connection-uuid --yes execute Re-import a connection's archived payloads, oldest first. Content-hash idempotent: rows already in the ledger skip, purged rows re-land — with feed invert now set on an account, its rows re-land sign-corrected under their original identities. A posted row that a fetch carried more than a week back under a new description, beside an original the ledger holds, skips as re-described, just as the sync skipped it (skipped redescribed in the summary). Commits per fetch, so an interrupted replay keeps its progress and re-running is safe. A replay re-derives transactions only. A loan or property balance and a brokerage's holdings describe the moment each fetch was made, and the live sync already recorded them, so a replay records no valuations and no holdings snapshots.

sections.heading: purser admin purge-retired-rows
sections.text: purser admin purge-retired-rows <path-or-uuid list batches purser admin purge-retired-rows <path-or-uuid --batch <created at dry-run report purser admin purge-retired-rows <path-or-uuid --batch <created at --apply execute Remove import rows that have no source fetch : rows an ingest path that no longer exists left behind, whose archived payloads are gone, so purge-feed-rows — which selects rows by fetch — cannot reach them. Manual QIF and CSV imports have no source fetch either, so the unit of removal is a creation batch : every row one import commits shares that transaction's created at timestamp. Without --batch, the command lists the account's batches, oldest first, each with its row count by status, its date range, and the audit actions recorded at the same instant — qif.import or csv.import marks a manual import. The audit trail is pruned after audit retention days, so an old batch may show none. Name the batch you mean with --batch, copying the timestamp exactly as listed (repeat the flag for several); the dry run then prints the counts and a sample of the rows. --apply (alias --yes) removes the batch by the ledger's own rules: - pending and expected rows are voided through the normal void path and stay as lineage; - posted rows are hard-deleted through the same guarded delete purge-feed-rows uses; - rows already void are left alone. A row with a live link refuses unless you pass --unlink: a proposed match is rejected, a confirmed match is undone (the bill it settled is expected again), and a merged transfer is unlinked — the other account's bank line comes back on its own account while this account's side goes with the batch. A row that was corrected after import, or that posts to another real account, always refuses. The apply run recomputes the plan and refuses if it no longer matches what the dry run showed. Each run is audited and emits account.retired rows purged; the raw feed archive is never touched.

sections.heading: purser admin rotate-key
sections.text: Re-encrypt every encrypted column under a new primary key. Run with both keys configured — PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY="<new ,<old " — and ciphertexts re-wrap without exposing plaintext; blind indexes and content hashes stay byte-identical. Drop the old key afterwards.

pages.title: Configuration
pages.description: Every PURSER_* environment variable, and which settings are runtime-editable in the admin UI.

sections.text: Purser is configured through PURSER environment variables (a .env file next to the process also works). A subset can be overridden at runtime in the admin UI ( Config - Settings ) or via the admin-scoped /config REST API; overrides persist in the database and win over the environment.

sections.heading: Required
sections.text: Variable Purpose --- --- PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY Fernet key for data encrypted at rest (raw bank envelopes, SimpleFIN access URLs, webhook secrets, narrative text). Every role command fails fast without it. Accepts comma-separated keys during rotation — the first key encrypts. Generate with purser keygen. Record it: encrypted data is unrecoverable without it.

sections.heading: Environment-only
sections.text: Infrastructure identity — never runtime-editable. Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- PURSER DATABASE URL postgresql+psycopg://purser:purser@localhost:5432/purser PostgreSQL DSN (psycopg v3 driver). PURSER PUBLIC URL http://localhost:8000 External base URL of the instance. Drives cookie security (https:// = secure cookies), the OIDC redirect URI, and the MCP endpoint's Host/Origin allowlist (requests for any other host get HTTP 421). The Helm chart derives it from the ingress host. PURSER HOST 0.0.0.0 Bind address. PURSER PORT 8000 Bind port. PURSER LOG LEVEL INFO Log level. PURSER MAX REQUEST BYTES 33554432 (32 MiB) Largest request body accepted. A bigger one is refused with 413 before it is read, signed in or not. 0 turns the limit off; a reverse proxy's own limit applies as well. PURSER DISABLE SCHEDULER false Set on the API process when a dedicated purser worker runs the jobs. The Helm chart sets it on the API pods when worker.enabled=true. PURSER WIDGETS DIR /app/widgets Directory of built MCP Apps widget bundles. PURSER STATIC DIR /app/static Directory of the built web UI (SPA) bundle. Dev falls back to frontend/dist when this has no index.html. PURSER DOCS URL unset Base URL of the deployed docs site. search docs returns absolute links when set, site-relative paths when not. PURSER SOURCE URL https://github.com/mlamoure/purser Where this instance's source code is published. GET /source redirects here, and the web UI footer and /llms.txt point to it. If you run a modified Purser, set it to your own published source (see Licence and notices).

sections.heading: Sign-in throttling
sections.text: Environment-only. Password sign-in (POST /auth/login) counts failures per email and per client address. At a limit, further attempts get 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds) and the password is not checked — see Security model. Counts live in memory, per process. 0 turns a limit off. Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- PURSER LOGIN MAX FAILURES 5 Consecutive failed sign-ins for one email (case-insensitive) before its attempts are refused. A successful sign-in resets it. PURSER LOGIN IP MAX FAILURES 20 Failed sign-ins from one client address, across all emails, before its attempts are refused. A success does not reset it. IPv6 addresses count per /64. PURSER LOGIN BACKOFF SECONDS 30 First lockout. It doubles with each further failure. PURSER LOGIN BACKOFF MAX SECONDS 900 Longest lockout. PURSER LOGIN FAILURE RESET SECONDS 3600 A count is forgotten after this long with no failure and no lockout in force. The client address is the connection's peer as uvicorn reports it. Behind a reverse proxy (Traefik, nginx, an ingress) every request comes from the proxy unless uvicorn is told to believe the proxy's X-Forwarded-For: set uvicorn's own FORWARDED ALLOW IPS variable to the proxy's address or network (default 127.0.0.1), and list nothing else — any address on that list can claim to be any client. Without it, the per-address limit counts the whole instance's failed sign-ins together, so a password spray pauses password sign-in for everyone until the lockout ends. SSO sign-in and agent tokens are unaffected.

sections.heading: Runtime-editable
sections.text: Environment value is the bootstrap default; the admin UI can override each of these live. Secrets (ai api key, oidc client secret, price api key) are write-only and encrypted at rest. Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- PURSER SESSION TTL DAYS 7 Absolute browser-session lifetime. PURSER SESSION IDLE HOURS 8 Sliding idle timeout for browser sessions. PURSER AUDIT RETENTION DAYS 90 Audit call/change rows older than this are pruned nightly (floor 7). PURSER TRANSFER AUTO LINK true Deterministic transfer auto-linking at import. Off = every candidate is confirm-first. PURSER PRIVACY PURCHASE false Agents receive payees as stable references (py ...), with descriptions, memos and bill names left out, unless a call asks for them with include. See Privacy and agents. PURSER PRIVACY AMOUNT false Agents receive no single-transaction or bill amounts unless a call asks for them. Totals and balances stay exact. PURSER AI PROVIDER none AI categorization provider: none, openai (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), or anthropic. PURSER AI BASE URL https://api.openai.com/v1 OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter...). PURSER AI API KEY unset Provider API key (write-only secret). PURSER AI MODEL unset Model name. PURSER AI REVIEW false Run the review pass server-side instead of waiting for a connected agent. Requires a configured provider on top of this — turning a provider on grants nothing by itself. PURSER REVIEW MAX AGE DAYS 90 Unreviewed transactions older than this are auto-marked aged by a nightly sweep, so the set cannot grow without bound. The count is reported rather than cleared silently. PURSER OIDC ISSUER unset OpenID Provider issuer URL (e.g. an Authentik instance). SSO enables when issuer, client id, and secret are all set; password login always remains as fallback. PURSER OIDC CLIENT ID unset OIDC client id. PURSER OIDC CLIENT SECRET unset OIDC client secret (write-only secret). PURSER OIDC AUTO PROVISION false Auto-create a member account for an SSO identity whose email matches no account, ignoring letter case (requires the provider to assert email verified). Off by default: such sign-ins get "account not provisioned" — pre-create users in the admin UI instead. PURSER GRAFANA URL unset Grafana base URL for deep links on tool responses; links omitted when unset. PURSER PRICE PROVIDER none Daily closes for hand-tracked positions: none (record closes by hand) or tiingo. The provider sees ticker symbols only. See Track holdings by hand. PURSER PRICE STALE DAYS 7 A hand-tracked position whose newest close is older than this many days is flagged stale (and price.stale fires once). 1 to 365. The price provider's API key has no environment variable on purpose: Purser is the party that sends it, so it lives only in Purser's encrypted settings ( Config - Prices , or PUT /config with price api key). It is write-only: responses report only price api key set. The SimpleFIN sync schedule (daily / every 12h / every 6h / hourly) is runtime-only — set it in Config - SimpleFIN .

sections.heading: Compose extras
sections.text: The bundled docker-compose.yml also reads POSTGRES PASSWORD (defaults to purser) for the sidecar database.

sections.heading: Licence and notices
sections.text: Purser is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 only (AGPL-3.0-only). The AGPL asks a network service to offer its source code to the people who use it, so every Purser screen, signed in or not, has a Source code link in its footer. sections.heading: Docker host binding
sections.text: The Compose file uses PURSER BIND ADDRESS (default 127.0.0.1) for its published host port. This is a Compose setting, not an application setting. Complete first-admin setup before exposing a remote interface. Compose also passes PURSER PUBLIC URL through to the application; use your HTTPS URL behind a reverse proxy.

pages.title: Events and webhooks
pages.description: The durable event stream, every event type, and HMAC-signed webhook delivery.

sections.text: Every notable state change appends a row to a durable events stream in the same transaction as the change itself. Consume it two ways: poll GET /events (read scope, cursor-paginated — the same stream the whats new MCP tool digests), or register webhooks.

sections.heading: Event types
sections.text: Type Fires when --- --- account.closed An account is closed (balancing adjustment posted, feed unmapped). account.deleted A duplicate account is hard-deleted via the guarded CLI. account.feed rows purged An account's feed-origin rows are hard-deleted via the guarded purge-feed-rows CLI. account.moved An account moves to a new path (PATCH /accounts/{id} with path). The payload carries the new path, the from path, and accounts moved — the account plus every account beneath it. account.reconciled An account is reconciled to a statement balance (adjustment posted when needed, claim recorded). Payload below. account.reopened A closed account is reopened. account.retired rows purged Import rows with no source fetch are removed by creation batch via the guarded purge-retired-rows CLI; the payload names the batches and counts transactions voided and transactions deleted. balance.drift A synced account's feed-reported balance disagrees with the ledger (once per drift episode); the payload's mode names the basis the delta is measured on, posted only or pending inclusive, and basis pinned: true appears only when that basis is the account's admin-set pin rather than learned. bill.late An expected transaction (a schedule instance, a manual bill, or an uncleared imported row) passes its date unmatched. forecast.shortfall The nightly forecast scan (07:15 UTC) projects an account that has a floor (min balance) below that floor within the next 30 days. Accounts without a floor are not scanned, even when projected below zero, and a forecast balance call never emits it. The floor is set at creation or later through PATCH /accounts/{id}, MCP update account or the app (write scope); the next scan uses the change, and clearing it stops the event. Once per account and first shortfall date: the payload carries account (the path), date (the first day below the floor), low (the 30-day projected minimum) and min balance. match.proposed The matcher proposes an expected-vs-imported pair. match.confirmed A match is confirmed. pending.vanished A pending imported transaction disappears from the feed with no posted successor (none of the same amount on its account within 7 days), and is voided. whats new counts these. position.updated A hand-tracked position changes: opened, renamed, an event recorded or reversed, or closed. The payload names the account path, position id, symbol and change (opened, renamed, recorded, reversed, closed); a rename adds the new name (null when cleared), and a recorded or reversed event adds kind, occurred on and quantity held (today's share count). price.fetch failed The price fetch (daily, or an admin's fetch-now) could not get or store some of a symbol's closes: the provider refused or failed a request, the store failed, or the answer carried closes out of range, which are dropped. Once per symbol per day for a failed request, and once more that day when closes were dropped, however often the fetch runs; the payload carries provider, symbol, status (the HTTP status, 200 for dropped closes, or null for a transport or store failure) and reason (a fixed phrase such as refused or 2 close(s) out of range dropped, or an exception's class name). Never the API key or a provider message. price.stale A symbol held by a hand-tracked position has a newest close older than the staleness threshold, or no close at all. Once per symbol per stale close: the payload's price as of (null when there is none) and stale days; a fresher close ends it, and a later stale close fires again. holding.unpriced A brokerage feed reports a held fund with no value (0 or none: a plan-only fund no provider prices) and no recorded price values it. Once per account and symbol when it turns unpriced, re-armed once the position was priced: the payload carries account (the path), symbol, quantity, as of (the date of the set it sits in) and unpriceable. record price under the fund's ticker values it; when unpriceable is true the feed sent a description instead of a ticker, and no recorded price can value it. holding.period open A brokerage account switched back to the feed still counts its hand-tracked holdings because no sync of it has arrived since, for longer than the price staleness threshold. Once per account and switch: the payload carries account (the path), since (the day of the switch) and stale days. Check the connection, or the account's mapping. recurring.price changed A recurring charge posts at a new amount. suggestion.created A new suggestion lands in the inbox (detected pattern, agent proposal, new-liability scan, a manual transfer confirm proposing a transfer link rule, or a match proposal's card — emitted beside match.proposed); dedup key is its fingerprint. The payload carries kind and source; a transfer link one also names account, counterparty account and payee, a match one account, label, expected date and posted amount. A repeat confirm or re-detection refreshes the open suggestion and emits nothing, and so does a match card re-opened by a new proposal of the same pair. suggestion.decided A suggestion is accepted, rejected or snoozed; the payload names the kind, the decision and, for accepts, what was created: result entity type schedule (active), rule (a transfer link rule, still a draft until you activate it) or match. A match card decided in the register (confirm, reject, or marking the bill paid with that row) emits it too; a card Purser withdraws emits nothing. sync.failed A SimpleFIN sync attempt fails. transaction.posted A transaction reaches posted. transfer.candidate An amount+window pair looks like a transfer but carries no signal (name, transfer link rule or transfer schedule). transfer.auto linked The deterministic auto-linker merges a pair: exact opposite amounts within the window, plus a signal — a name signal, a transfer link rule declaring the pair (whose window days may set that pair's window, and whose payee scope, when it has one, a leg's payee must match), or a transfer schedule's instance covering it. The payload's signal names the first that applies: rule:<rule id , name or schedule:<schedule id . transfer.confirmed A transfer pair is merged by an explicit confirm. A split loan payment's payload also carries remainder (the interest/fee amount) and remainder category; those keys are absent on an ordinary transfer. transfer.absorbed A late-arriving counterpart is absorbed into an existing transfer. transfer.unlinked A transfer link is undone. valuation.recorded A property/loan valuation or holdings snapshot is recorded. variance.threshold A matched pair's amount variance exceeds the threshold.

sections.heading: account.reconciled payload
sections.text: Emitted once, when a reconciliation is recorded. Dry runs and retries emit nothing. The event's entity id is the account. Amounts are decimal strings in the ledger's sign (a card is negative when owed), except statement balance, which is the figure as the statement prints it: { "path": "liabilities.card", "currency": "USD", "reconciliation id": "8d1f6c0e-5b7a-4f0e-9c3d-2a6b1e4f7c90", "as of": "2026-09-30", "basis": "posted", "statement balance": "425.0000", "target balance": "-425.0000", "ledger balance": "-400.0000", "adjustment": "-25.0000", "adjustment tx id": "c4a2e9b1-7d3f-4e86-b5a0-91f2d6c8e3b7" } ledger balance is the balance on as of in that basis before the adjustment. adjustment is "0.0000" and adjustment tx id is null for a clean reconcile. A reconciliation that later goes out of balance emits no event; reads report it. See Reconcile an account.

sections.heading: Webhooks
sections.text: Manage subscriptions with admin scope: - POST /webhooks — subscribe a URL to event types (wildcards supported); an optional per-subscription secret is encrypted at rest. A new subscription receives events from its creation onward — for history, replay GET /events instead. - GET /webhooks, DELETE /webhooks/{id} — list and remove. - GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries — delivery log with response codes. - POST /webhooks/deliver — process due deliveries immediately (the worker also does this on schedule).

sections.heading: Delivery contract
sections.text: Each delivery is an HTTP POST of the event JSON with: Header Content --- --- X-Purser-Event The event type. X-Purser-Delivery Unique delivery id (dedupe on this). X-Purser-Signature Hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the subscription secret. Only when a secret is set. Verify by recomputing the HMAC over the raw request body . Non-2xx responses retry with exponential backoff — 1, 4, 16, and 64 minutes — then the delivery is marked failed after 5 attempts. Replay missed events any time from GET /events with your last cursor.

sections.heading: balance_history
sections.text: One account's balance over time, in a single call. period = 30d 90d 1y all (or pass start and end for an explicit window, which wins). Adaptive density chosen server-side and reported in density — 30d is a true daily series. low/high are the lowest and highest END-OF-DAY balance over EVERY day with activity in the window, not just the returned points, so they stay true under downsampling, and the order of one day's rows (pay posted before its deductions) never creates one; movers names the biggest balance movements. Full per-transaction resolution is behind series uri. This is the historical counterpart to forecast balance; for the whole portfolio use net worth. Never reconstruct a balance series by walking transactions. include: fields to return although the user's privacy defaults withhold them — any of payee, description, amount, external ids. sections.heading: confirm_transfer
sections.text: Merge an opposite-amount pair into one transfer (write scope). Posted cross-account pairs within 3 days that carry a transfer signal (a transfer keyword, the counterparty account's name, a transfer link rule, or an instance of an active transfer schedule) auto-link at import and in the nightly sweep; pairs WITHOUT a signal stay candidates and need this explicit confirm. A row already matched to an expected transfer still pairs with that transfer's other side, and the match moves onto the merged transfer. Split loan payment: when the cash leg pays more than the principal leg the loan account shows (the rest is interest or fees), pass remainder category = the expense category for that part (e.g. expenses.fees.interest). Both bank legs keep their exact amounts, the difference becomes one posting to that category, and no full-payment loan leg is invented. The incoming (principal) amount must be positive and smaller than the outgoing (cash) amount; the result then also carries remainder and remainder category. Never automatic; unlinking the transfer restores both bank rows. An ordinary confirm also proposes a transfer link rule for this account pair, scoped to the payee, in the suggestions inbox (suggestion id in the result; repeat confirms refresh the same one). It links nothing until a human accepts it with decide suggestion and confirms its projected link count when activating the rule; reject it to never see it again. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- outgoing id string yes — incoming id string yes — remainder category string \ null no null

sections.heading: create_schedule
sections.text: Create a bill/income schedule (e.g. from a parsed statement email). It is created active. When you are acting on your own initiative rather than on the user's request (a pattern you noticed), pass propose=true: it lands as a suggestion for the user to decide, and is refused when the account already has a schedule for that payee or counterparty (the error names it). note (200 characters or fewer) is a proposal's evidence for the person deciding it, such as the statement line you read; it shows on the suggestion's card. A direct create keeps no note. rrule is RFC 5545 (FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=6,20 is semi-monthly); dtstart (YYYY-MM-DD) anchors it — pass the last real occurrence so anchor-sensitive rules count from it. amount is the schedule account's leg (negative = money out); required for amount type=fixed, the fallback for amount type=estimated (estimate basis last rolling avg 3 rolling avg 12 from confirmed matches, or counterparty balance = pay the counterparty's full reported balance, for card payments). A recurring TRANSFER — card payment, loan payment, 529/IRA contribution — names the other real account as counterparty account instead of a category; its instances are two-leg expected transfers. The schedule is itself the signal that links its bank rows (the same two accounts, exactly the instance amount, both sides within 3 days of the instance — also when the sides post on different days), and the merged transfer settles the instance once. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- name string yes — account string yes — rrule string yes — amount string \ null no null amount type string no "fixed" payee string \ null no null category string \ null no null dtstart string \ null no null estimate basis string \ null no null autopost policy string no "wait for match" counterparty account string \ null no null note string \ null no null propose boolean no false

sections.heading: decide_suggestion
sections.text: Decide a suggestion (write scope). accept applies the draft exactly as shown: a schedule suggestion becomes an active, materialized schedule; a transfer link suggestion becomes a DRAFT rule (rule.projected links is how many past pairs it would link) that links nothing until a human activates it on the Rules page, confirming that count. edit then accept applies it with edits (schedule draft fields: name, rrule, dtstart, amount, amount type, estimate basis, payee, category, counterparty account, autopost policy; transfer link: amount exact as a decimal string, window days 0 to 14, effective from YYYY-MM-DD). A match suggestion: accept confirms the proposal (match{id,state,variance} in the result) and reject rejects it for good — the matcher never proposes that pair again; it has nothing to edit, and a proposal already gone withdraws the suggestion with an error. reject is durable — reject scope=counterparty means never suggest this payee/counterparty on this account again (for a transfer link: this account pair, any payee; a match rejects exactly); snooze hides it until snooze until (YYYY-MM-DD, default 30 days). Nothing auto-accepts. include: fields to return although the user's privacy defaults withhold them — any of payee, description, amount, external ids. Ask only for what the user's question needs; a response names what it withheld in withheld. sections.heading: forecast_balance
sections.text: Deterministic balance projection with every move explained. The events array IS the chart: each entry carries the running balance after, so the step line and the narration come from the same data. low is the projected minimum and end balance the balance on the last day; min balance is the account floor (null when unset). coverage says what the line is made of — schedules active == 0 means a flat line by construction, not a quiet month, and suggestions open how many candidate schedules await a decision (list suggestions), and matches pending how many instances are left out as already paid: an open match proposal names a bank row that is in the balance (matches pending net, their net, only when nonzero; list unmatched names each one's proposed posted id and match on that pair confirms it). Events flagged projected are rule occurrences past the materialized horizon (no instance row yet); overdue ones are still due and land today. An event with basis 'statement' carries a card statement balance someone recorded (record statement balance) and one with 'override' an amount the user set; without basis the amount is the schedule's own (fixed or an estimate — a card payment's default is the card's current balance, not its statement). An estimated event may carry range {low, high}: the min and max of its schedule's newest six settled amounts and its own; low.range {low, high, low date} is the projected low with every ranged event at its worst and at its best, and the headline names what could take the account under its floor. days is 1..365. events lists the largest movements that fit the response budget, always including the one that makes the low; materiality (a decimal string) lists only movements at least that large. omitted {count, net} accounts for every movement not listed, so start balance + the listed amounts + omitted.net = end balance; truncated is true when the budget, not materiality, left one out. daily uri is the full daily series: resources/read, or read series where only tools are forwarded. Renders as the forecast widget in MCP Apps hosts. Looking BACKWARD is balance history(account, period). include: fields to return although the user's privacy defaults withhold them — any of payee, description, amount, external ids. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- account string yes — days integer no 30 materiality string \ null no null include array of string \ null no null

Loan/property accounts report their latest valuation instead of the postings sum (marked balance method='valuation'); brokerage accounts add their latest holdings market value on top of it (balance method='postings+holdings'). Both carry the overlay's balance as of date. A reconciled account carries reconciliation: its latest reconciled date and basis, and whether the ledger still matches the statement on that date (difference = ledger minus statement target, ledger sign; nonzero means a later write moved it). include: fields to return although the user's privacy defaults withhold them — any of payee, description, amount, external ids.
